newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cemig sales seen up 3.4 pct in '97.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cemig sales seen up 3.4 pct in '97.

text.p: Minas Gerais state-owned power distributor Cemig said its electricity sales are expected to grow on average 3.4 percent this year to 34.7 million megawatts per hour.
Between now and 2010, electricity sales are also forecast to grow 3.4 percent a year, said Luis Carlos Fonseca, Cemig's market department advisor.
Preliminary figures showed an increase of 3.7 percent in electricity sales in 1996 to 33.6 million megawatts per hour against the 32.4 million megawatts per hour in 1995, Fonseca added.
He attributed the rise to soaring residential and commercial electricity consumption which jumped 8.9 percent and 8.6 percent last year, respectively.
He said residential electricity sales rose due to the ongoing anti-inflation plan coupled with eased credit which boosted consumption of electrical appliances among Brazilians.
